standard_prerequisites.name: Ideals of a valuation ring correspond to ideals of the value group
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in both halves of the counted proof (lines 12323 and 12330)
standard_prerequisites.use: Translates the ideal-theoretic chain conditions into statements about the value group.

standard_prerequisites.name: The value group of a discrete valuation ring is the integers
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the first half of the counted proof (lines 12320-12325)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces explicit generators of the ideals and hence a principal ideal domain.

core_obligations: One direction: with the valuation normalised to the nonnegative integers, describe the ideals as the sets of elements of valuation at least n, note that each is generated by an element of valuation exactly n, and conclude that the ring is a principal ideal domain (proof lines 12320-12326).

Conversely, for a Noetherian valuation ring whose value group has a positive element, apply the ascending chain condition to the ideals of the value group to conclude that the group is a copy of the integers, and check that the ring is not a field only in that case (proof lines 12328-12342).
proof_roadmap: Read Noetherianity off an explicit description of the ideals for discrete valuations (proof lines 12319-12326).
Use the correspondence with ideals of the value group in the other direction (proof lines 12328-12342).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a valuation ring is Noetherian exactly when it is a discrete valuation ring or a field (statement lines 12313-12317). The proof does not quote the classification of Noetherian valuation rings: in one direction it uses the explicit description of the ideals of a discrete valuation ring to exhibit generators and get a principal ideal domain, and in the other it translates the ascending chain condition into the value group and deduces that the group is a copy of the integers (proof lines 12319-12342). The translation between ideals and the value group in the converse is the content, and the author writes both directions out. H2.
